data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["A large service could deliberately emulate divergent incentives (e.g., separate teams with independent release cycles).","Independent operators might have convergent incentives (e.g., all prioritize cost, choosing the same cheap provider)."],"overturn_conditions":["If the large service intentionally creates internal operational diversity, the emergent barrier is not unique to decentralization.","If independent operators converge on identical practices, the emergent barrier collapses."],"shared_structure":["Divergent incentives and schedules create operational diversity.","Monoculture in centralized systems enables simultaneous propagation of single bugs."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_008"],"transfer_claims":["Just as genetic diversity in a population protects against a single pathogen, operational diversity in a network protects against a single bug.","The claim transfers: a monoculture crop is more vulnerable to a blight than a polyculture, even if the monoculture has more individual plants."]},"claim":"Decentralization is more resilient not because of redundancy count, but because independent operators have divergent incentives and maintenance schedules, creating an emergent causal independence barrier that a centrally managed large service cannot replicate even with strict internal redundancy.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The large service intentionally staggers updates and uses multiple configuration management systems, replicating the temporal diversity.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Independent operators converge on a single managed service or library, creating a hidden monoculture.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The decentralized network's diversity is only apparent; all operators use the same underlying open-source framework with the same bug.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"In a large service, centralized configuration management and synchronized update schedules create a monoculture where a single bug propagates to all replicas simultaneously.
